questions.prompt: What does debouncing a search box mean?
options: Run the search on every keystroke, but on a background thread
Run the search at most once per second, even while the user is still typing
Wait until the user stops typing, then run the search once
Run the search only when the user presses Enter
questions.explanation: Debouncing means "wait until the user stops typing, then do the work once": typing `task` triggers one search instead of one for `t`, `ta`, `tas` and `task`.

questions.prompt: With the WPF `DispatcherTimer` debounce (300 ms), put the events from one keystroke to the search in order.
steps: The user types and the `SearchText` setter runs
The user stops typing and 300 ms pass with no more setter calls
`Tick` fires: the timer is stopped and `ApplySearch()` runs
questions.explanation: Every setter call stops and restarts the timer; only when no keystroke arrives for the full interval does `Tick` fire, stop the timer and call `ApplySearch()`.

questions.prompt: With a 300 ms debounce, the user types `T`, `Ta`, `Tas`, `Task`, each keystroke less than 300 ms after the previous one, then stops. How many times does `ApplySearch()` run?
options: Once, after the user stops typing
Twice, at the first and last keystroke
Never, because the timer was stopped
questions.explanation: Each keystroke cancels the previous countdown and starts a new one, so the timer only reaches `Tick` 300 ms after the last keystroke, and `ApplySearch()` runs exactly one time.

questions.prompt: Why is calling `_searchTimer.Stop()` right before `_searchTimer.Start()` the heart of the debounce?
options: It makes the timer tick twice as fast while the user types
It cancels the pending countdown and starts a fresh one
It clears `SearchText` so the next search starts from empty
`Start()` throws an exception if the timer is already running
questions.explanation: Stop-then-Start cancels the pending countdown and schedules a fresh one. As long as keystrokes keep arriving, the timer never reaches `Tick` and the search never runs.

source.section: Why Stop() before Start() is critical

questions.prompt: In the WinForms version, where is the debounce countdown restarted?
questions.explanation: In WinForms, `textBoxSearch_TextChanged` calls `_searchTimer.Stop()` to cancel the previous countdown and `_searchTimer.Start()` to restart it; when typing stops, `Tick` fires and the search runs once.
